import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('dacomp-072.csv')

# Filter to relevant columns and suppress confidential data
agg_df = df[['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 'decision_speed_category', 
              'overall_performance_score']].copy()

# Add group sizes for suppression check
group_sizes = agg_df.groupby(['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 
                             'decision_speed_category']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# Merge group sizes back
agg_df = pd.merge(agg_df, group_sizes, on=['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 
                                          'decision_speed_category'])

# Aggregation function with suppression
def safe_agg(group):
    if len(group) < 5:
        return np.nan
    return group.mean()

# Build hierarchical roll-up
def build_rollup(df):
    # Top level - performance_tier
    tier_totals = df.groupby('performance_tier')['overall_performance_score'].agg(
        ['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
    tier_totals.columns = ['performance_tier', 'tier_avg_score', 'tier_count']
    
    # Middle level - performance_tier + specialization
    tier_spec_totals = df.groupby(['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization'])['overall_performance_score'].agg(
        ['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
    tier_spec_totals.columns = ['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 
                               'spec_avg_score', 'spec_count']
    
    # Detailed level - full hierarchy
    full_totals = df.groupby(['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 
                            'decision_speed_category'])['overall_performance_score'].agg(
        ['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
    full_totals.columns = ['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 
                          'decision_speed_category', 'detail_avg_score', 'detail_count']
    
    return tier_totals, tier_spec_totals, full_totals

# Execute roll-up
tier_totals, tier_spec_totals, full_totals = build_rollup(agg_df)

# Validation function
def validate_hierarchy(tier_totals, tier_spec_totals, full_totals):
    # Check tier sums
    tier_spec_check = tier_spec_totals.groupby('performance_tier')['spec_avg_score'].sum() == \
                     tier_totals.set_index('performance_tier')['tier_avg_score']
    
    # Check spec sums
    full_check = full_totals.groupby(['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization'])['detail_avg_score'].sum() == \
                 tier_spec_totals.set_index(['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization'])['spec_avg_score']
    
    return tier_spec_check, full_check

# Run validation
tier_spec_check, full_check = validate_hierarchy(tier_totals, tier_spec_totals, full_totals)

# Identify inconsistencies

inconsistent_specs = full_check[~full_check]

# Prepare output

    'tier_totals': tier_totals,
    'tier_spec_totals': tier_spec_totals,
    'full_totals': full_totals,
    'inconsistent_tiers': inconsistent_tiers,
    'inconsistent_specs': inconsistent_specs
}

# Display results

print("\n=== TIER + SPECIALIZATION LEVEL ===")
print(tier_spec_totals.to_string())
print("\n=== FULL HIERARCHY LEVEL ===")

print(inconsistent_tiers)
print("\nSpecification-level inconsistencies:")
